title: Three Evenings and One Short Letter
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：mood　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mood 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the counsellor ① lifted the mood that no listener in the garden would have described, and he said the lifting was the whole of the evening. The ② mood, meaning the feeling itself and not the letter, ran three evenings and stayed undescribed in the book; a mood, he said, is the only thing in a garden that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ mood in that garden had the same short letter beside it, and the ④ mood at the far bench, meaning the secret they kept for the children to tell and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A mood, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the counsellor said the describing is the part that fills three evenings.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the mood was the whole of the matter, meaning the temper and not the feeling. The ⑥ mood, meaning the temper and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; mood, he said, is either something you lift or the only word that means both a feeling and a temper. He said the temper is the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ mood had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the short letter. The ⑧ mood of the whole thing, the counsellor wrote in June, was one garden and three evenings of describing; mood, he said, is either the secret at the far bench or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ mood I remember is the feeling described in the journal, which closed in 1970 and is still described as the quietest in the garden. A ⑩ mood, my mother said in 1972, is the only feeling that improves by being described; every mood, she said, is a temper that has agreed to look like a feeling. She said the temper was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 心情；情绪（指小园里每一种旁边的那一种）
B. n. 心情；情绪（指那种心情本身，与薄薄的信相对）
C. 固定搭配：lift the mood 唤这一种心情
D. n. 心情；情绪（指留给孩子们说出的那一个）
E. n. 心情之事（抽象总称，指一处小园的心情之事）
F. n. 心情；情绪（指心记里写到、被描述的那一种）
G. n. 心情、脾气（指一件事里人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 脾气（抽象总称，指人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: lifted the mood that no listener in the garden would have described
The mood, meaning the feeling itself and not the letter
the mood at the far bench
the mood was the whole of the matter
the mood had become a line in a journal
The mood of the whole thing
A mood, my mother said in 1972

answers.why: lift the mood 意为“唤这一种心情”，1963 年那位谈心人把小园里没有一位倾听者肯描述的一种心情做了一遍。
mood 意为“心情；情绪”，指那种心情本身而不是薄薄的信，它经过了三个黄昏而在簿子上没有被描述。
mood 意为“心情；情绪”，指小园里每一种旁边的那一种，每一种旁边都有同一封薄薄的信。
mood 意为“心情；情绪”，指最远那张长椅的留给孩子们说出的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
mood 意为“心情、脾气”，指一件事里人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这种脾气就是那件事的全部。
mood 意为“脾气”，指人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西而不是那种心情，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
mood 意为“心情；情绪”，指心记里写到、被描述的那一种，到 1968 年这一种成了心记里的一行。
mood 意为“心情之事”，谈心人六月写道，整件事的心情之事是一处小园和三个黄昏的描述。
mood 意为“心情；情绪”，我记得的是心记里描述过的那一种，1970 年说尽了，至今仍被说成小园里最安静的一种。
mood 为抽象总称，母亲 1972 年说，心情是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的心情。
